brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.requirement: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching
requirements.evidence: Configurator enforces geometry: a spike requires the three cells around a vertex to be present (spike:0#0,0|1,-1|1,0 at 95.7,0,0), while a notch/drawer requires an empty cell beside two touching bases. A vertex is shared by exactly three cells, so the spike's vertex has no empty neighbor cell to host a notch. Closest achievable is both on the same base cell (piece:0,0,0;full) at adjacent vertices: spike at its east vertex and drawer frame notch:0#-1,0#notch0 with drawer:0#0,-1#cut on its south side, both attached to the same central cluster but not the same vertex. No socket exists for co-located spike+drawer.

finish.summary: Build demonstrates the clash: placed spike at 0,0|1,-1|1,0 and notch-drawer (drawer:0#0,-1#cut) on same central cell 0,0 but at different vertices because the same-vertex condition is geometrically impossible in Hex Cluster. Check_build is clear apart from expected LOOSE_BODY/OPEN_CAP_FACE warnings.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
